messages.subject: Filming permit RBC-FP-6619 granted: Tannery Row
messages.snippet: Dear Ms Thackeray,  Filming permit RBC-FP-6619: Tannery Row, Tannery Row  Thank you for your application of 2 November...
messages.body:
Dear Ms Thackeray,

Filming permit RBC-FP-6619: Tannery Row, Tannery Row

Thank you for your application of 2 November 2026. I am pleased to tell you that Rookhaven Borough Council grants permission for Greyfriars Wharf Productions to film 'The Lamplighter's Daughter' at Tannery Row on 23, 24 and 25 November 2026, subject to the conditions below. Please make sure your unit manager and marshals have a copy before the first day.

Conditions

1. Hours. Filming, rigging and de-rigging on Tannery Row may take place between 07:00 and 20:00 only. Generators and lighting must be off and the street clear by the end of those hours.

2. Parking. Six residents' bays and four pay-and-display bays outside numbers 2 to 18 may be suspended on each day covered by this permit. The production must place the council's suspension notices on the bays at least 48 hours before each day and remove them at the end of the last day.

3. Insurance. The production's public liability cover of at least 10 million pounds, as on the certificate supplied with the application, must remain in force for every day of filming.

4. Pedestrians. A clear footway of at least 1.5 metres must be kept at all times, with marshals at each end of any section where equipment is placed on the pavement.

5. Residents' access. Residents, carers and deliveries must be let through at all times. Vehicle access to driveways must not be obstructed for more than five minutes.

6. Noise. No amplified playback after 19:00. Generators must be the silent type listed on the application and placed where shown on the location plan.

7. Waste. All waste, cable ties and gaffer tape must be removed each day. The council will charge for any clean-up it has to carry out.

8. Neighbour notices. Every household on the notification list must be told of the dates in writing before the first day, by the means set out in the production's notification procedure.

9. Refuse collection. Bridge Street is closed for resurfacing from 23 November, so Tannery Row carries the diverted refuse collection round on Wednesday 25 November 2026. This permit does not cover filming or any parking suspension on Tannery Row on Wednesday 25 November 2026; the bays must stay open for the collection vehicles all that day. Filming on 23 and 24 November is not affected.

10. Listed buildings. Nothing may be fixed to the frontages of numbers 7 to 11, which are listed. Lamps on stands only.

11. Emergency services. Access for emergency vehicles must be kept clear at all times; the production must comply at once with any instruction from the police, fire service or council officers.

12. Changes. Any change to the dates, hours or extent of the filming must be agreed in advance with the council's filming office. Amendments made by the council are published in the permit feed and govern over this letter.

13. Charges. Parking suspension charges are invoiced after filming at the rates in the council's fee schedule in force on the day.

If you have any questions about these conditions please reply to this message or ring the filming office on 01632 960 718.

Yours sincerely,

Desmond Quilliam
Filming officer, Rookhaven Borough Council
